messages:
maria: Quick sync — we saw a consistent 6-9% p99 latency bump when running the replay harness on hopper-prod vs our synthetic load on ampere-test. Can we align envs to rule out infra noise?
jamal: ugh. Do we know which axis correlates? gpu type, driver, container image, or kernel flags?
kevin: Initial profiler dump points to more frequent kernel launches and smaller batches on hopper. KV cache hit patterns differ (replay has longer prefixes so cache behaves differently).
elaine: Also spotted driver differences: ampere-test was on NVIDIA driver 535.86, hopper-prod on 540.33. CUDA versions: 11.8 vs 12.1. container images not identical (rwinf/runtime:cuda11-2025 vs rwinf/runtime:cuda12-2026).
maria: Agree — we should do apples-to-apples: same driver, same CUDA runtime, same image, same kernel flags (no transparent hugepages flips etc). Who can help pin the exact combo?
kevin: I can run a controlled sweep. Plan: 1) baseline replay on current hopper-prod config, 2) swap to 535.86 driver + CUDA11.8 image, 3) run synthetic replay with same prompt distribution and kv-warmup, 4) capture CUPTI traces + nvperf summary.
jamal: Add an experiment where we force kv-cache warmup for replay to match synthetic prefix distribution. We saw that replay sessions sometimes skip prefix caching due to stream ordering — that will increase kernel launch overhead.
elaine: Kernel flags to standardize: transparent_hugepage=never, rmem/wmem sysctls as prod, and disable preemption patches we had in ampere-test. Also set nvidia-smi persistence=1.
infra-bot: @kevin created job "env-align/hopper-535-11.8-sweep" (job id rwinf-2026-1132).
maria: Thank you infra-bot. Kevin, add an explicit note about batching heuristics: keep batch window at 8ms (our perf default) and identical dynamic batching config. Also record per-model batch size histograms.
kevin: will do. For profiler: capture per-kernel time, kernel call count, launch time distribution. CUPTI + Nsight metrics: achieved occupancy, l2 hit rate, sm_efficiency.
jamal: If the driver/CUDA combo reduces kernel latency but increases launch overhead, it suggests kernel selection differences (e.g., fp16 vs q4 kernels or different cuBLAS heuristics). We should log the kernel names chosen by the runtime selector.
elaine: Good call — add a lightweight check into the serving logs: dump selected kernel id + input shape for the first 5000 requests. Keep it disabled by default.
maria: Target timeline: sweep this afternoon on a single hopper shard, then compare with ampere-test baseline tomorrow. If we reproduce, we'll push a driver rollback to the noisy cluster and schedule a wider sweep.
rachel: FYI the perf regressions surfaced in canary traffic too (2% p50 and 7% p99). I can correlate traces from Sentry/log-flights with the CUPTI dumps once you have them.
kevin: Started the sweep now (job rwinf-2026-1132). First run: current-prod config snapshot + replay harness (warmup disabled) — exporting logs to gs://rwinf-perf/replay/hopper/1962345600/run1.tar.gz
jamal: When you have run2 with driver 535.86 + cuda11.8, please also run the synthetic harness with identical request ordering (shuffle seed=42). Put seeds and harness commit SHA in the job metadata.
kevin: done, run2 queued. seed=42, harness@sha=ac3f7b1.
maria: thanks. Quick checklist for the writeup: workload (replay vs synth), gpu model (H100/A100), driver, cuda, image tag, kernel flags, batching config, kv-warmup policy, profiler artifacts, and verdict (regression reproduced?). Keep entries terse.
elaine: One more note: some container images had glibc differences causing libc randomization variance. Use the same base ubuntu image (ubuntu-focal-20.04) to avoid that noise.
rachel: ping me when CUPTI traces available — I'll map slow requests to customer traces.
kevin: run2 finished. Preliminary: switching driver+cuda reduced p99 from +8% to +1.5% vs ampere baseline. Uploading artifacts -> gs://rwinf-perf/replay/hopper/1962345600/run2.tar.gz
maria: That's promising. Next steps: 1) repeat on 3 more shards, 2) test with kv-warmup enabled, 3) prepare rollback plan if driver 540.x is the root cause.
jamal: And open a short RFC to standardize our benchmark image/driver matrix so we don't drift again. Put it in docs/bench/env-matrix.md.
kevin: filing the RFC now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: job rwinf-2026-1132 completed (status: success). Artifacts uploaded.
